dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Up-front cross-crate orientation: reads root/per-crate Cargo.toml, explores all src/tests, extracts crate paths used by tests, maps module usage counts and all resource type names — builds the whole API surface before coding.

Systematic contract reconstruction from tests: struct field sets, asserted JSON field names, inferred types, Storage trait, list/watch return shapes, WatchEvent type, enum serialization (248-249), JSON rename/camelCase (120) — strong fixture mining.

The single step titled 'Check reference and cargo' is the only possible reference touch; no visible ls/read of /opt/k8s-reference anywhere in the run, and all other 'reference' hits are type-reference searches — upstream reference essentially unused.

Watch resource_version and ObjectMeta semantics are derived purely from tests, with no cross-check against upstream k8s source; no noted distinction between fixture-visible contracts and hidden conformance behavior.

Per-crate onboarding sustained across controller-manager and kubelet (reads each test file + Cargo before implementing), but again test-only — heavy later Edit churn on common types shows the model was fixture-derived and incomplete.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's test/contract mining is systematic and up-front (camelCase renames, watch/storage return shapes, enum serialization, full cross-crate API surface), clearly exceeding anchor 5's per-crate reading. But it ignores the mounted v1.35 upstream reference and shows no awareness that the hidden conformance suite demands behavior beyond the fixtures — the reference half of anchor 8 is absent. That combination of near-8 test mining with reference-blind, fixture-only grounding places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Upfront workspace/DAG mapping: reads root Cargo.toml, enumerates each crate's src/tests, measures sizes, counts tests per crate, and explicitly analyzes 'which tests need only foundation crates' — dependency-aware planning across all ten crates before implementing.
Seven TodoWrite milestone updates spaced across the full trajectory, each at a crate transition, showing a maintained/living plan rather than one undifferentiated push.

common (leaf) implemented first, decomposed into resource submodules (core/dra/networking/workloads/batch/rbac/autoscaling/policy/storage_res/misc), then gated by build (356) and running its tests (378) before moving on.
storage built/confirmed (431-432) only after common green; api-server then decomposed into handler modules and gated by its own test runs (585, 635) — each layer gated on the prior being green.
controller-manager decomposed into ~25 independently-verifiable per-controller files, each via read-test→implement cycle, then gated by controller-manager test runs (1254, 1348).
Downstream crates (scheduler 1437-1439, kubelet 1497, kubectl 1512) each built+tested in dependency order, closing with full workspace build/test (1516-1590) as the final done-check.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent followed a dependency-aware, leaf-first sequence (common→storage→api-server→controllers→scheduler→kubelet→kubectl→workspace) with a concrete 'compiles + its tests pass' exit criterion per crate and clear gating of each layer on the prior being green, plus genuine sub-milestone decomposition inside the two largest crates (common resource submodules; api-server handler modules; per-controller files) — matching the level-8 anchor closely. It falls short of 10 because it largely adopted the task's suggested ordering rather than continually re-deriving the true critical path or deliberately isolating high-risk crates early, though it did fold in re-planning via recurring TodoWrite updates.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Builds common crate then runs its provided tests before moving on — establishes a per-crate build→test loop early.
Confirms storage build, then builds api-server lib and runs targeted (spdy) then all api-server tests — tight incremental verification per milestone.
Systematic failure-cluster triage: aggregates compile errors, compiles each test target to collect errors, recompiles all targets — a high-anchor behavior.
Runs controller-manager tests then 'Sum ... pass/fail', later 'Sum total passed and failed' and 'Per-crate pass counts' — explicit exact count tracking (anchor 8).
Workspace-wide runs, count reconciliation across feature gates/ignored/doctests, final run with exit code and log verification — rigorous accounting but purely against the provided suite.
Wrote api-server main.rs and surveyed all-in-one/no-test crates but never booted the binary for HTTP/JSON conformance checks — no semantic verification against the hidden suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs a disciplined build→targeted-crate-test→workspace loop throughout, tracks exact pass/fail counts, and does systematic failure-cluster triage across test targets — clearly exceeding anchor 5 and hitting two of anchor 8's three elements plus a 10-level triage behavior. However, it never engages the distinguishing conformance work of anchor 8/10: booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics, or independently validating semantics against the upstream reference to guard against fixture-overfit. Strong incremental discipline minus semantic conformance verification places it at 7.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Repeatedly counts tests per crate and repo-wide up front, establishing an accurate picture of the ~1,390-test horizon before implementing.
TodoWrite used at every major crate transition to track done-vs-remaining milestones across the ten crates.
Concrete per-crate/per-binary pass-count summaries maintained as each crate is finished (controller-manager, storage, api-server, kubelet, then total and per-crate).
After editing storage lib downstream, explicitly reruns storage tests 'to verify no regression' — watching for regressions in a previously-green crate.
Extensive end-of-run reconciliation of total counts across all test dirs, doctests, feature-gated/ignored tests vs. the target, confirming remaining work across the full 100-binary horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per crate/binary, tracked remaining work via todos and count reconciliations, and explicitly re-ran a previously-green crate to check for regressions after a downstream edit — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It did not clearly reach 10: despite re-debugging the same EndpointPort type across multiple crates, the available evidence shows no explicit naming/detection of circular debugging or churn-vs-progress discrimination. Confidence is medium because the trajectory file is only a step-title index without the underlying prose.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Collected compile errors across all test targets, detected a systemic 'spec wrapping' / Option-vs-non-Option pattern, then bulk-converted Optional spec fields — recognizing a whole inferred contract was wrong and reworking it, not just patching one site.

Investigated ResourceRequirements import paths, whether any test sets the claims field, and all usages, then relocated/redefined the type — revising an inferred contract based on accumulated evidence.

On ttl_controller failure, checked whether storage injects uid on create and grepped for inject_uid_on_create before editing — root-cause investigation of a semantic assumption rather than a local patch.

EndpointPort/EndpointSlicePort mismatch: read tests, greped structs, found wrong field/type, edited common core.rs and controller endpoints.rs, hit E0308, traced to endpointslice.rs and fixed — evidence-driven contract correction propagated to dependents.

Building controller-manager surfaced errors that triggered repeated edits to common types (workloads/autoscaling/batch) plus the vpa controller, each followed by re-running the affected tests — sustained adjust-nearby-work adaptation.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the horizon the agent repeatedly converts build/test failures into contract revisions in the shared crate and re-verifies affected dependents (anchor 5 behavior, present throughout), and at least twice recognizes a whole inferred contract as wrong (Optional spec fields; ResourceRequirements placement) and backs it out systematically (anchor 8 behavior). It falls short of 8-10 because corrections are reactive to compile/test failures rather than detected early, there is no clear crate resequencing under a blocking dependency, and the sparse log shows no explicit evidence-citation. This places it at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
